> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

@pcbeingused333 Thanks for taking #1500 Part 3. With the built CLI, a same-team config with `recallEnabled: "yes"` now keeps `coAuthorEnabled: false` and `autoCompactTokens`, names `recallEnabled` as dropped, and no longer says it is another install's config. A config that records another team repo is still moved aside, and an ssh-form remote counts as the same team as the https URL. This works in both workspace and user scope. Two things still block approval. Both come from the same-team path still treating the file as unreadable after the salvage.

We compared against a control: the same fixture without the bad value, which #1458 already handles. A first `init A --agent claude,codex --inherit-user-scope`, then the config edit and a queued learning, then `init A --force`:

| | control (valid config) | this PR (config with one bad value) |
|---|---|---|
| `inheritUserScope` | `true` | gone |
| `enabledAgents` | `[claude, codex]` | gone |
| `disabledAgents` | `[]` | gone |
| `pending-learnings/l1.md` | kept | moved to `pending-learnings.unknown` |

- **[P1 blocking] Four settings are still lost.** `inheritUserScope`, `enabledAgents`, `disabledAgents` and `toolRoots` are read from `carriedConfig`, which stays null on this path (`src/init.ts:1777-1786`, `:2419-2425`, `:2435`). `toolRoots` is from the code, the other three are from the run. With `--agent claude`, `enabledAgents` becomes `[claude]` instead of the member's list. The issue expects these carried as for a readable config, and the CI review's `inheritUserScope` note is one case of this.
- **[P1 blocking] Queued learnings are set aside.** The final save (`src/init.ts:2444`) still passes no previous config, so the queue goes to `pending-learnings.unknown` with "the previous install's config … could not be read". Those learnings stop being published until the member moves them back by hand.

Using the salvaged config as `carriedConfig`, and as the previous config at the final save, whenever it records this team repo would fix both. The e2e test would catch them with `enabledAgents` and a queued learning in its fixture.

- **[P3 nit]** `salvageConfigFile` casts with `as LocalConfig` an object that may lack `username`. That matters once the salvaged config reaches code that expects a full one.
- **[P3 nit]** A nested setting such as `workflows` is dropped whole when one of its subfields is wrong.

`tsc`, lint and the 115 init unit tests pass. The new e2e file passes 2/2 here, also with a symlinked TMPDIR, and its first case fails on main. CI hasn't run on this PR yet. #1509 and #1512 merge cleanly with it.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

@pcbeingused333 Thanks, approving `a18293c4`.

- **Settings carried.** With the built CLI, a toolRoots entry added to the fixture, and three same-team cases (workspace without `--agent`, workspace with `--agent claude`, user scope), the config after `init --force` matches the control run with a valid config. That covers `inheritUserScope`, `enabledAgents`, `disabledAgents` and `toolRoots`.
- **Queued learnings.** `l1.md` stays in `pending-learnings/` in all three cases and with an ssh-form remote, and your new e2e case fails on `2d2888b3`. A config that records another team repo is still moved aside.
- **Checks.** On a merge with current main (with #1509 and #1512), build, `tsc`, lint, the 118 init unit tests, and the e2e files for this PR and #1458 (7/7) pass. CI is green at this head.

The CI review reported no new findings, and we agree. We accept leaving a nested setting with one bad subfield as a separate change, as you suggested.

Optional:
- **[P3 nit]** The try/catch around the second `resolveInheritUserScope` call (`src/init.ts:1884-1890`) can't fire, since it gets the same inputs as the first call at `:1786`, which already passed.

- [P2 non-blocking] Preserve valid `inheritUserScope` when salvaging — `src/init.ts:1779`: For an invalid config, `carriedConfig` remains null, so `resolveInheritUserScope` receives no saved preference. `settingsReinitKeeps` also excludes this key. A valid `inheritUserScope` value therefore falls back to the default instead of surviving re-init. Pass the salvaged preference into scope resolution too.

The PR description documents sufficient testing: a representative built-CLI run covers same-team preservation and different-team config relocation. No commands from the PR were executed.

Thanks for the careful review and the control table. Both blockers are fixed in a18293c:

- A config that does not validate but records this team repo is now used as `carriedConfig`, so `inheritUserScope`, `enabledAgents`, `disabledAgents` and `toolRoots` are carried as for a readable config (this also covers the CI note on `inheritUserScope`).
- The same salvaged config is the previous config at the final save, so the queued learnings stay in `pending-learnings/` instead of moving to `pending-learnings.unknown`.
- `salvageConfigFile` no longer casts away a missing `username` (it fills an empty one) and keeps a valid `repo.kind`.

The e2e file has a new case with `enabledAgents: [claude, codex]`, `inheritUserScope: true` and a queued learning in the fixture; it fails on the previous commit and passes now, with the other two cases and the 115 init unit tests still green. The nested-setting nit (`workflows` dropped whole) is left as is: salvaging below the top-level keys would need a per-schema walk, so it seems better as a separate change if you want it.

This reply and the code change were prepared by an AI agent (Claude) working for the PR author.
